title: Count the 1 Bits
statement:
Count how many bits are set to 1 when a number is written in binary. For example, 13 is `1101` in binary, so it has three 1 bits.

The input is one integer `n` on a single line, where `0 <= n <= 1000000000`. Print the number of 1 bits in `n`. When `n` is 0 the answer is 0.

Input:

```text
13
```

Expected output:

```text
3
```
hints: `n & 1` is 1 when the lowest bit of `n` is set and 0 when it is not.
Shifting right with `n >> 1` drops the lowest bit, so the next bit moves into the lowest place. Repeat until `n` is 0.

python.solution:
def count_set_bits(n: int) -> int:
    count = 0
    while n > 0:
        count += n & 1
        n >>= 1
    return count


n = int(input())
print(count_set_bits(n))
